Cigarette Smoking
There are over 4000 chemicals produced from a cigarette, with some chemicals being 
known carcinogens. Nicotine is primarily metabolized in the liver, eliminated by the 
kidneys, and can easily cross the placenta with fetal concentrations that are generally 
15% higher than maternal levels.69 Nicotine consumption during pregnancy has been 
consistently associated with low neonatal birth weight, pre-term delivery, and sponta-
neous abortion.15 Smokers have a 40% higher risk of pre-term births than non-­
smokers.70 Recent research has shown a correlation between smoking during 
pregnancy and childhood asthma, obesity, and sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS).71 
These risks are associated with maternal smoking in late pregnancy.72 If women who 
smoke become pregnant, they should be advised to discontinue cigarette smoking.
Caffeine
Caffeine is metabolized more slowly in pregnancy and passes readily through the 
placenta to the fetus.69,73 Women who consume 200 mg of caffeine daily are twice as 
likely as women who consume no caffeine to have a miscarriage.17 According to the
